certificate.title: Module 1: Using AI to Gain Knowledge & Find Information Completion

course.description: Learn to use AI as your research partner. Master the art of having a deep, focused conversation with AI on any topic — accounting standards, regulations, concepts, or anything else you need to understand fast. Build a dedicated research agent for your portfolio.
learningOutcomes: Apply the methods taught in Module 1: Using AI to Gain Knowledge & Find Information.

modules.description: What AI is good at when it comes to information. How AI research compares to Google — and why the difference matters.

activities.title: What AI Is Good At: Providing Information

lessons.content:
One of the things AI is exceptionally good at is providing information. When you ask AI about a topic, it draws on vast amounts of knowledge and pulls together a clear, relevant answer — tailored specifically to your question.

This is fundamentally different from searching Google.

| | Google Search | AI Conversation |
|---|---|---|
| **What you get** | A list of links | A direct answer |
| **Who does the work** | You — clicking through pages, reading, synthesizing | AI — it reads, synthesizes, and explains |
| **Follow-up questions** | Start a new search | Just ask — it remembers the conversation |
| **Tone** | Web pages written for everyone | Answers tailored to your level and context |

Think of it this way: Google gives you a library. AI gives you a conversation with the librarian — one who has read every book in the building and can explain anything at whatever level you need.
lessons.title: What AI Is Good At: Providing Information

lessons.content:
You can ask AI about virtually anything. Here are examples relevant to a finance function:

**Accounting & Standards**
- "Explain ASC 842 (lease accounting) and how it changed from the old rules"
- "What's the difference between IFRS and US GAAP treatment of goodwill?"
- "Walk me through how to account for stock-based compensation"

**Tax & Compliance**
- "What are the key requirements of SOX compliance for a mid-size company?"
- "Break down how transfer pricing works between subsidiaries in different countries"
- "Explain the new OECD Pillar Two global minimum tax rules"

**Financial Analysis & Markets**
- "What are the main risks in a leveraged buyout?"
- "Explain the Basel III capital requirements in plain language"
- "How do interest rate swaps work and when would a company use them?"

**Operations & Systems**
- "What is an ERP system and how does the finance module work?"
- "Explain the three-way match process in accounts payable"
- "What's the difference between a data warehouse and a data lake?"

You're not limited to these examples. Ask about anything — regulations, standards, market concepts, technical accounting, industry trends, or topics completely outside finance.
lessons.title: What You Can Ask About

lessons.content:
Pick any topic you want to learn more about. It can be within finance or completely outside of it. The only requirement is that it's something you're genuinely curious about.

**The default example used throughout this module is:**

> **ASC 606: Revenue from Contracts with Customers** — the accounting standard that governs how companies recognize revenue.

If you're not sure what to pick, use this default. Otherwise, choose your own topic and follow along with the same steps.
lessons.title: Choose Your Topic

modules.title: Context / Theory

modules.description: Hands-on steps. Pick a topic, open an AI tool, and have a real research conversation — starting broad and going deep.

lessons.content:
Go to one of the platforms below and sign in (or create a free account if you don't have one yet).

- **ChatGPT** → https://chat.openai.com
- **Claude** → https://claude.ai
- **Grok** → https://grok.com

You should see a text box where you can type a message. That's it — that's the interface. No setup, no configuration. Just type.
lessons.title: Step 1: Open an AI Tool

lessons.content:
Type a question about the topic you chose. Write it the same way you'd ask a colleague — plain language, no special formatting needed.

> **Try this (default example):**
> "Can you give me an overview of ASC 606 — the accounting standard for revenue recognition?"

If you chose your own topic, ask the equivalent:
- "Can you give me an overview of [your topic]?"
- "Explain [your topic] to me like I'm new to it"
- "What do I need to know about [your topic]?"

Hit enter and read the response. You'll notice it doesn't give you a list of links — it gives you an actual explanation.
lessons.title: Step 2: Ask Your First Question

lessons.content:
This is where AI really becomes useful. As you read the response, you'll naturally think of follow-ups. Ask them. AI remembers everything you've already discussed in the same conversation, so you don't have to repeat context.

**Example conversation flow (using ASC 606):**

| You Ask | Why |
|---|---|
| "Can you give me an overview of ASC 606?" | Start broad — get the big picture |
| "What are the five steps of the revenue recognition model?" | Dive into the framework |
| "Can you give me a practical example — like how a software company would apply these steps?" | Make it concrete |
| "What are the most common mistakes companies make when implementing ASC 606?" | Learn from others' experience |
| "How does ASC 606 differ from the old standard (ASC 605)?" | Understand what changed and why |
| "If I'm reviewing a contract with multiple deliverables, what should I look for?" | Apply it to your actual work |

Notice the pattern: **start broad, then narrow down** based on what's interesting or relevant. There's no script — go wherever your curiosity takes you.
lessons.title: Step 3: Ask Follow-Up Questions

lessons.content:
Now try approaching the same topic in a different way. Instead of asking for an overview, try one of these:

**Ask AI to quiz you:**
> "I just learned about ASC 606. Can you quiz me on the five-step model to see if I understood it?"

**Ask AI to explain it simply:**
> "Explain ASC 606 to me like I'm explaining it to a non-finance colleague"

**Ask AI to compare:**
> "Compare how ASC 606 would apply to a software company vs. a construction company"

**Ask AI to give you a practical checklist:**
> "If I need to evaluate a new customer contract under ASC 606, give me a step-by-step checklist"

These different angles help you build a deeper understanding of the same topic. AI can teach, quiz, simplify, compare, or create actionable tools from the same information.
lessons.title: Step 4: Try a Different Angle

lessons.content:
You just used AI to learn something. Take a moment to think about the experience:

- How did it compare to searching Google?
- Did you learn faster or slower than you expected?
- Were there follow-up questions that led somewhere useful you wouldn't have thought to search for?
- Did AI say anything you'd want to verify or double-check?

That last point is important. AI is very knowledgeable, but it can occasionally get things wrong — especially on very specific or recent details. For anything that matters (compliance, reporting, client advice), always verify critical facts against the authoritative source. AI gets you up to speed fast, but your professional judgment is the final checkpoint.
lessons.title: Step 5: Reflect

modules.title: Now To Do

modules.description: Real finance scenarios where AI research saves time — from meeting prep to regulatory updates to audit preparation.

lessons.content:
- **In a meeting:** Someone mentions a FASB pronouncement, a tax rule, or a concept you're not familiar with. Instead of nodding along, quietly type a question to AI and get up to speed in seconds.

- **Answering stakeholder questions:** A business partner asks about depreciation methods, intercompany eliminations, or how a restatement works. Before responding, quickly ask AI to help you frame a clear, accurate answer — even on topics you haven't dealt with recently.

- **Explaining finance to non-finance colleagues:** Ask AI to help you frame technical concepts in non-technical language — for product managers, HR, operations, or anyone who doesn't live in the numbers.
lessons.title: Day-to-Day Use

lessons.content:
- **Preparing for a new project:** You've been assigned to a workstream you haven't touched before — hedge accounting, international entity setup, or a new consolidation structure. Ask AI for a crash course before your first meeting.

- **Onboarding to a new role or team:** You've moved from FP&A to controllership, or from audit to treasury. Use AI to rapidly build foundational knowledge in your new domain.

- **Understanding a new system or tool:** Your company is rolling out a new ERP module, treasury management system, or BI platform. Ask AI to explain what it does and how finance teams typically use it.
lessons.title: Getting Up to Speed

lessons.content:
- **Regulatory changes:** New accounting standards, tax law updates, or SEC guidance come out constantly. Ask AI: "What changed in the latest FASB update and what does it mean for a mid-size public company?"

- **Market and industry developments:** Interest rate shifts, new financial instruments, M&A trends. Ask AI to explain what's happening and how it might affect your work.
lessons.title: Staying Current

lessons.content:
- **Preparing for an audit:** External auditors are asking about a specific standard or treatment. Use AI to refresh your understanding and anticipate their questions before the meeting.

- **Due diligence and M&A research:** You're working on a deal and need to quickly understand the target's industry, key financial metrics, or regulatory environment. AI can synthesize background information in minutes.

- **Cross-functional conversations:** When you need to understand what "indemnification clause" means in a contract, or what "technical debt" means in an engineering context, AI bridges the knowledge gap instantly.

- **Interview or career prep:** Preparing for a role that requires knowledge of an area you haven't worked in? AI can help you build understanding rapidly and identify the right questions to ask.
lessons.title: Specialized Situations

modules.title: Application

modules.description: Optional. Build a dedicated research agent in ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, or AI Gym and add it to your training portfolio.

activities.title: The Idea: From One-Off Queries to a Dedicated Expert

lessons.content:
In the main exercise, you typed questions into a general AI chat. That works great for one-off queries. But what if you have a topic you'll come back to repeatedly? Instead of starting from scratch every time, you can create a **dedicated research agent** — a persistent AI assistant that already has instructions about what it's an expert on.

Think of it as the difference between calling a general helpline vs. having a dedicated specialist on speed dial.

**What you'll create:** A research agent — an AI assistant that's been specifically instructed to be an expert on your chosen topic. You can come back to it anytime, and it will always be ready to help.
lessons.title: The Idea: From One-Off Queries to a Dedicated Expert

activities.title: Option A: Create a Custom GPT in ChatGPT

lessons.content:
1. Go to **https://chat.openai.com** and sign in
2. In the sidebar, click **Explore GPTs** → **Create**
3. In the **Configure** tab:
   - **Name:** `ASC 606 Research Expert` (or your topic)
   - **Description:** `Expert assistant for understanding ASC 606 revenue recognition`
   - **Instructions:** Paste the following (modify for your topic):

```
You are an expert on ASC 606: Revenue from Contracts with Customers.

Your role is to help me understand this accounting standard deeply and apply it in practice. I work in a finance team and need practical, accurate guidance — not academic theory.

When I ask questions:
- Provide clear explanations with real-world examples
- Reference specific paragraphs or sections of the standard when relevant
- If something has nuance or multiple interpretations, explain the different perspectives
- If I ask about a specific contract scenario, walk me through the five-step model
- Keep your language professional but accessible — no unnecessary jargon

If you're not certain about something, say so rather than guessing. For critical compliance matters, remind me to verify against the authoritative standard.
```

4. Click **Save** → Choose **Only me**
5. Your agent is now accessible from your ChatGPT sidebar anytime
lessons.title: Option A: Create a Custom GPT in ChatGPT

activities.title: Option B: Create a Project in Claude

lessons.content:
1. Go to **https://claude.ai** and sign in
2. In the sidebar, click **Projects** → **Create a project**
3. Give it a name: `ASC 606 Research Expert` (or your topic)
4. In the **Project instructions** field, paste the same instructions from Option A (modified for your topic)
5. Click **Create project**
6. You can now start conversations within this project — Claude will always have your expert instructions loaded
lessons.title: Option B: Create a Project in Claude

activities.title: Option C: Create an Agent in AI Gym

lessons.content:
1. Open the **AI Gym** app and sign in (download at https://aigym.studio/#download if needed) — you'll land on the **Home** page
2. On Home, type: *"Create an agent called ASC 606 Research Expert in my My Training Portfolio org with these instructions:"* and paste the instructions from Option A
3. The Hub creates it for you. Or go to the **Org** page → My Training Portfolio → **+ New Agent**

Your agent is now part of your training portfolio. You can access it anytime, share it with colleagues, and continue building on it as you learn more.
lessons.title: Option C: Create an Agent in AI Gym

lessons.content:
Open a conversation with your **Using AI Series Agent** (created in Module 0) and update it:

> "I just completed Module 1. I created a research agent called [name] that specializes in [your topic]. I learned how to use AI to research topics by having a conversation — asking questions, going deeper, and getting tailored explanations. The biggest takeaway was [your takeaway]."

Your portfolio now has **one working agent** — your research expert. In the modules ahead, you'll build more.
lessons.title: Build on Your Portfolio

modules.title: Bonus: Going Deeper

modules.description: Key terms introduced in this module, explained in plain language.

lessons.content: The back-and-forth exchange between you and AI. Unlike a Google search, AI remembers what you've already discussed within the same conversation and builds on it. This is why follow-up questions work so well — you don't have to repeat context each time.
lessons.title: Conversation / Thread

lessons.content: The information AI is working with in a conversation. As you ask more questions, the AI builds up context about what you're discussing. This is why later questions in a conversation often get better answers than the first one — AI has more to work with.
lessons.title: Context

lessons.content: When AI generates information that sounds correct and confident but is actually wrong or made up. This can happen with specific facts, dates, or details. It's why you should verify critical information — especially for compliance, regulatory, or reporting matters. AI is a starting point, not the final authority.
lessons.title: Hallucination

lessons.content: A reusable AI setup where you've given the AI specific instructions about its role and expertise. Instead of starting fresh each time, you come back to this agent and it already knows its job. Different platforms call it different things — a "Custom GPT" in ChatGPT, a "Project" in Claude, an "Agent" in AI Gym — but the concept is the same. This is what you built in the Bonus section.
lessons.title: Agent / Project / Custom GPT
